rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ships resemble lofty mountains because they rise above the water, and their sails add further height.
rows.anchor: أي الجبال الشاهقة بما لها من العلو في نفسها عن الماء

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil says Arabs call anything elevated an ʿalam.
rows.anchor: وقال الخليل : كل شيء مرتفع عند العرب فهو علم .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can still the wind that carries ships, leaving them unable to travel; people acknowledge that wind's command belongs to Him alone.
rows.anchor: التي يسيرها وأنتم مقرون أن أمرها ليس إلا بيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb ẓalla describes the ships remaining, even at night; its daytime sense is fitting because daylight is when people expect power to relieve hardship.
rows.anchor: ولعله عبر به مع أن أصله الإقامة نهارا لأن النهار موضع الاقتدار على الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rawākid means fixed and settled, with no movement.
rows.anchor: ثوابت مستقرات من غير سير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their stillness on the sea's surface is conspicuous and firm, as the spelling and vocalization indicate.
rows.anchor: ثباتا ظاهرا بما دل عليه إثبات اللامين وفتح لامه الأولى للكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At sea the polytheists call on God alone and admit their idols cannot help, but on land they associate partners and act as though the ships' fate were no sign.
rows.anchor: لا تغني في البحر شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ships' motion and stillness are signs of God's exclusive power; sailors' unanimous appeal to Him alone shows that knowledge of His perfection is innate and other gods are plainly false.
rows.anchor: من الإجماع على التوجه في ذلك إليه خاصة والانخلاع مما سواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic qualities call for patience in hardship and gratitude in ease, rather than panic, ingratitude, or abandoning the truth when circumstances change.
rows.anchor: أي في الرخاء وإن كثر مخالفوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sincere believer reflects on the signs, draws lessons from them, and uses them to sharpen inner sight.
rows.anchor: فهو يستملي منها العبر ويجلو بها من البصيرة عين البصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet grieves intensely over their refusal, but the rhetorical question denies that he can make deaf, blind, deeply misguided people hear or find guidance by himself.
rows.anchor: أي وحدك من غير إرادة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their deafness is an image for God having sealed their understanding with the lead of misery.
rows.anchor: وقد أصممناهم بما صببنا في مسامع أفهامهم من رصاص الشقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their blindness is an image for coverings of dullness and loss over their inner sight; their chosen blindness accompanies their deafness.
rows.anchor: الذين أعميناهم بما غشينا به أبصار بصائرهم من أغشية البلادة والخسارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those in manifest error are naturally immersed in it, and their error is so evident that no one can miss it.
rows.anchor: أي بين في نفسه أن ضال وأنه محيط بالضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The point is that hearing and guidance belong to God, while the Prophet's duty is only to convey the message.
rows.anchor: ليس شيء من ذلك إليك , بل هو إلى الله القادر على كل شيء , وأما أنت فليس عليك إلا البلاغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God takes Muhammad away from among them by death or otherwise, He will punish them afterward; the Prophet's presence is why punishment is delayed.
rows.anchor: من بين أظهرهم بموت أو غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God may show the Prophet the punishment promised to them while he is among them; God has power in either case.
rows.anchor: أي من العذاب وعبر فيه بالوعد ليدل على الخير بلفظه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling punishment a promise uses a favorable word while conveying harm through its context, so the expression encompasses both.
rows.anchor: وعبر فيه بالوعد ليدل على الخير بلفظه وعلى الشر بأسلوبه فيعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One of the two outcomes was eternally known not to occur; God honored Muhammad by sparing him what he would dislike in his community before his death.
rows.anchor: عن أن يريه شيئا يكرهه في أمته حتى قبض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These alternatives exemplify God's power over what would be impossible for anyone else; many verses make the same point.
rows.anchor: فالآية من أدلة القدرة على المحال لغيره وهي كثيرة جدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding alternatives place listeners between fear and hope, emphasize that God alone knows the unseen, and imply that punishment is inevitable and only He controls harm and benefit.
rows.anchor: أفهم السياق وإن كان شرطا أن الانتقام منهم أمر لا بد منه , وأنه لا قدرة لأحد على ضرهم ولا نفعهم إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must diligently hold to all revelation received from the start of his prophethood, in dealing with them and in everything else.
rows.anchor: من حين نبوتك وإلى الآن في الانتقام منهم وفي غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation is a broad, clear, straight route to the goal, so steadfast adherence leaves opponents unable to harm the Prophet.
rows.anchor: موصول إلى المقصود لا يصح أصلا أن يلحقه شيء من عوج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation is great honor, admonition, and explanation; calling honor dhikr points to remembrance and observance of its law as the source of that honor.
rows.anchor: عبر عن الشرف بالذكر للتنبيه على أن سببه الإقبال على الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an honors Quraysh, the Arabs, and all its followers because it came through one of them in their language and gives them knowledge, distinction, and leadership.
rows.anchor: قريش خصوصا والعرب عموما وسائر من اتبعك ولو كان من غيرهم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says this leadership remains with Quraysh while two people remain, provided they uphold the religion; those who uphold it are honored in heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( لا يزال هذا الأمر في قريش ما بقي في الناس اثنان ما أقاموا الدين )

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi reports al-Daḥḥāk from Ibn ʿAbbās: Muhammad did not name his successor when asked until this verse came, then answered that it would be Quraysh.
rows.anchor: روى الضحاك عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا سئل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī infers from that report that Muhammad understood Quraysh would inherit Muslim rule after him through the honor of the Qur'an revealed to one of them.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فهم من هذا أنه يلي على المسلمين بحكم النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The community will become a source of knowledge for people everywhere about religious and worldly concerns, despite once being regarded as weak and ignorant; it will also be questioned about its duties and response to revelation.
rows.anchor: أي تصيرون في سائر أنواع العلم محط رحال السائلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To answer the claim that the Merciful would have prevented idol worship if He disapproved, the Prophet should examine revelation and see whether it leaves any ambiguity about divinity belonging to another.
rows.anchor: شبهتهم الوهمية القائلة { لو شاء الرحمن ما عبدناهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accessible earlier messengers were Moses, Jesus, and Israel's prophets, whose teaching is preserved in the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, and prophetic books.
rows.anchor: إنما هو لموسى وعيسى ومن بينهما من أنبياء بني إسرائيل عليهم الصلاة والسلام الحافظ لسنتهم من التوراة والإنجيل والزبور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their followers altered texts, so the Prophet should have them recited and let the Qur'an judge them; agreement among the books exposes distortions and resolves ambiguous passages through clear ones.
rows.anchor: فإنهم إذا قرؤوها بين يديك وعرضوها عليك علمت معانيها وفضحت تحريفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī says this request has the same purpose as a verse in Sūrat Yūnus.
rows.anchor: فالمراد من هذا نحو المراد من آية يونس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh and his followers call Moses ‘sorcerer’; the distant form of address signals that, though present, he is far from their hearts.
rows.anchor: فرعون بالمباشرة وأتباعه بالموافقة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This episode rebukes Quraysh: earlier deniers called a messenger a sorcerer yet asked him to pray when punishment struck, contradicting their claims of steadfastness, reason, and fairness.
rows.anchor: والتعبير بهذا توبيخ لقريش بالإشارة إلى أنهم وغيرهم ممن مضى يرمون الرسول بالسحر ويقرون برسالته عند الحاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī recounts that during famine Abu Sufyan asked Muhammad in Medina to pray for his people, citing kinship and their suffering; after Muhammad prayed, rain relieved them, recalling the years like Joseph's famine.
rows.anchor: أتى أبو سفيان بن حرب إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالمدينة الشريفة فقال

rows.speaker: أبو سفيان بن حرب
rows.claim: Abu Sufyan tells Muhammad that he came as a kin, his people are perishing, and asks him to pray to God for them.
rows.anchor: يا محمد إنك قد جئت بصلة الأرحام وإن قومك قد هلكوا فادع اللهلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Moses a sorcerer is incompatible with asking him for prayer, just as believing someone a sorcerer would make such a request irrational.
rows.anchor: وهو وصفه بالسحر وطلب الدعاء منه يمنع اعتقاد أنه ساحر , واعتقاد أنه ساحر يمنع طلب الدعاء منه عند العاقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request to pray ‘by the covenant You have’ refers to God's favor toward Moses and his promise to grant relief to believers and humiliation to those who persist.
rows.anchor: من أنه يفعل من وضعها ورفعها على ما تريد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their emphatic promise to become steadfastly guided after relief sounds credible to any listener, especially from a prominent person.
rows.anchor: أي اهتداء ثابتا يصير لنا وصفا لازما عند كشف ذلك عنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As soon as God removes the affliction, they break their pledge again, repeatedly and without shame or fear.
rows.anchor: أي فاجؤوا الكشف بتجديد النكث بإخلاف بعد إخلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beyond breaking his word, Pharaoh summons his people to spread his message widely so no one thinks he has converted; he fears the signs have shaken their hearts.
rows.anchor: أي الذين لهم غاية القيام معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh appeals to common identity and their strength, then claims that his exclusive rule over Egypt leaves no one entitled to challenge him.
rows.anchor: بأنهم لحمة واحدة , ومستنهضا بوصفهم بأنهم ذوو قوة على ما يحاولونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh portrays Israel's departure from his control as rebellion against the rightful ruler and disorder, excusing his broken pledge under pressure.
rows.anchor: أن غلبته على بني إسرائيل ومقاهرته على إخراجهم من تحت يده بغى على من له الملك فتكون فسادا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading leaves Miṣr without tanwīn, marking it as a proper name; tanwīn can imply diminishment, contrary to Pharaoh's intended grandeur.
rows.anchor: ولم يقرأ بالصرف ليكون نصا على مراده من العلمية , ولأن المصر يطلق على المدينة الواحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh says the rivers run beneath him because he had branched canals toward his gardens and palaces and could direct them wherever he wished, a power no one else had.
rows.anchor: من تشقيق الخلجان إلى بساتينه وقصوره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Do you not see?’ asks them to perceive inwardly that no one should rival him; Biqāʿī calls this the speech of a weakened man whose ties have come undone.
rows.anchor: أي الذي ذكرته لكم فتعلموا ببصائر قلوبكم أنه لا ينبغي لأحد أن ينازعني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Judgment Day every community, both successful and doomed, is gathered separately, kneeling in terror and waiting like a litigant before a judge for an unavoidable verdict.
rows.anchor: باركة على الركب رعبا واستيفازا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every community has persisted in the good or evil it made habitual, without turning back.
rows.anchor: أي مصرين عليه غير راجعين عنه من خير أو شر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ‘book’ is the revelation sent through God's messengers, whose rulings God will carry out in judgment.
rows.anchor: أي الذي أنزلناه على ألسنة رسلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book speaks against people by truth: its general classifications of unbelief, sin, and obedience match their particular deeds exactly, without addition or omission.
rows.anchor: فيطبق ذلك على ما عملتموه فإذا الذي أخبر به الكتاب مطابق لأعمالكم لا زيادة فيه ولا نقص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book also speaks in believers' favor through grace, multiplying a good deed tenfold and beyond.
rows.anchor: الحسنة بعشر أمثالها إلى ما فوق ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Judgment aligns the book of revealed rulings with the record of deeds: God enforces the former against the latter.
rows.anchor: فما حكم به كتاب الإنزال أنفذه الكبير المتعال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In response to the question of who records countless deeds over long periods, God explains how He preserves them despite people's denial of recorders and revelation.
rows.anchor: وكانوا ينكرون أمر الحفظة وغيره مما أتت به الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands angels to copy or transfer everything people do in speech, action, and intention.
rows.anchor: أي نأمر ملائكتنا بنسخ أي نقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naskh may mean transfer generally, or copying from an original such as the tablet of dispositions or the Preserved Tablet so that the record matches each person's deeds.
rows.anchor: وإن كان النقل من أصل فهو إشارة إلى لوح الجبلات

rows.speaker: الناس
rows.claim: Biqāʿī notes a popular belief that each person's forehead records the good or evil that will befall them.
rows.anchor: ومن المشهور بين الناس أن كل أحد يسطر في جبينه ما يلقاه من خير أو شر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God enters believers who trust and do righteous deeds into His mercy, meaning nearness, honor, great reward, and a good final home; angels greet them with peace.
rows.anchor: أي تقريبه وإكرامه بجليل الثواب وحسن المآب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is manifest triumph because it has no obscurity, blemish, or deficiency, unlike worldly success whose causes were hidden from all but the certain.
rows.anchor: الذي لا يخفى على أحد شيء من أمره , لأنه لا يشوبه كدر أصلا ولا نقص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers who reject innate and rational recognition of truth enter God's curse, even if they performed good deeds without faith.
rows.anchor: أي ستروا ما جلته لهم مرائي عقولهم وفطرهم الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are asked whether messengers came and whether minds, visible miracles, and revealed verses gave them guidance toward the truth.
rows.anchor: وأخلق لكم عقولا تدلكم على الصواب من التفكر في الآيات المرئية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive ‘were recited’ allows any reciter, stresses repeated delivery, and portrays the verses as reaching them forcefully beyond an impartial person's ability to dismiss.
rows.anchor: أي تواصل قراءتها من أي تال كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rather than becoming humble at revelation, they sought greatness over God's messengers and signs.
rows.anchor: أي فتسبب عن تلاوتها التي من شأنها إيراث الخشوع والإخبات والخضوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mujrimūn evokes people who sever what deserves connection; their entrenched wrongdoing is manifest loss.
rows.anchor: أي عريقين في قطع ما يستحق الوصل , وذلك هو الخسران المبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage uses ḥatbāk: mercy for believers implies the curse of disbelievers, while the rebuke of disbelievers implies the honor of believers, highlighting each side's standing.
rows.anchor: ذكر الإدخال في الرحمة أولا دليلا على الإدخال في اللغنة ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's promise is true and unavoidable, including resurrection; even an ordinary king would keep a promise, and breaking one would contradict divine wisdom.
rows.anchor: أي ثابت لا محيد عنه يطابقه الواقع من البعث وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour is the promise's central focus and the place where divine wisdom, majesty, and beauty will be displayed fully, so it admits no doubt.
rows.anchor: التي هي مما وعد به وهي محط الحكمة فهي أعظم ما تعلق به الوعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They claim not to know what the Hour is, although knowledge of it is rooted in human nature and a slight reminder makes God's power apparent to the heart.
rows.anchor: أي الآن دراية علم ولو بذلنا جهدنا في محاولة الوصول إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call the Hour only a guess out of arrogance, although its reality is innate; at times fitra prompts belief, while desire and ignorance lead them to deny it, or they belonged to two factions.
rows.anchor: سموا ذلك ظنا عنادا واستكبارا , فقالوا مستأنفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first ẓann means belief, while the second means conjecture; they add that they are not certain because ẓann may also mean knowledge.
rows.anchor: كان الظن الأول بمعنى الإعتقاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their denial does not conflict with ‘it is only our worldly life’: at times they assume resurrection, at others appetite and ignorance make them insist it will not come, or they were two groups.
rows.anchor: لأن آخرها مثبت للظن , فكأنهم كانوا تارة يقوى عندهم
